A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Prompt Injection as Role Confusion, with matching methods and experiments. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–K in both versions.

before.justification: v3 reports original CoT Forgery attack results, agent exfiltration experiments, role-probe measurements, and controlled analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and adds granular style ablations and an instruction-hierarchy failure prediction experiment.

M1.justification: The CoT Forgery construction and tag-controlled linear role-probe training remain unchanged in Sections 3.1, 4.1, and Appendix G. The additions apply the existing probes and analyze attack variants rather than revise the proposed methods.

E1.justification: Appendix K adds evaluation on 160 prompts from Geng et al. (2025), each containing conflicting system and user instructions. This adds behavioral instruction-hierarchy testing beyond v3's positional probing experiment. Existing dataset and task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The new Appendix K experiment compares the Systemness/Userness ratio regression against token-count and mean-activation-norm regressions and shuffled-label controls. These comparisons are absent from v3; the original attack comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added instruction-hierarchy experiment uses pre-generation gpt-oss-20b activations, 160 conflicting-instruction samples, logistic prediction, and AUC evaluation. Appendix D adds independent top-1/top-5 lexical, pronoun, and syntactic interventions. These are new experimental protocols, without a stated revision to the retained experiments' settings.

E4.justification: Appendix D extends the existing broad destyling analysis with feature-specific ablations and a qualitative analysis of leading-space tokenization. Appendix K adds a predictive validity test beyond prompt injection. The original logic ablations, layer analyses, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain bootstrap confidence bands and template-clustered regression standard errors and p-values. v5 supplies a 95% confidence interval for its new AUC result, but does not document a changed uncertainty-estimation practice, seed policy, or repeated-run count; the additional interval accompanies the new result.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports lexical, pronoun, and syntactic ablation ASRs of 42%, 58%, and 26%, respectively. Appendix K adds AUC 0.74 versus controls at 0.59, 0.60, and 0.52. Existing plotted values and matched tables are retained. Sections 5.1–5.2 also correct trend descriptions from monotonic to near-monotonic without changing the plots.

T1.justification: The role-probability definitions and mathematical formulation of the linear probes remain unchanged. The added Systemness/Userness ratio is an empirical prediction feature; v5 introduces no new formal proposition, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: role confusion explains prompt injection, role probes measure it, confusion predicts attack success before generation, and CoT Forgery exploits this mechanism. The rewritten abstract and added supporting experiments do not redefine those claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds explanations emphasizing syntactic structure and sparse lexical or whitespace cues as drivers of role perception. Section 5.1 locally softens the inference from confirming a causal pathway to supporting it. Existing model-scope and linear-probe limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The introduction and Appendix A replace redacted access information with an explicit project/code address and describe standalone probe-training and attack-analysis notebooks. Appendix B directs readers to the codebase for the demo and prompts. These improve documented access; actual external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Yong and Bach (2026), Self-jailbreaking, to the discussion of reasoning attacks and to the bibliography. The broader positioning relative to prompt-injection, instruction-hierarchy, probing, and defense research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 rewrites the abstract and makes targeted explanatory edits in the introduction, discussion, and Appendix K. It adds acknowledgements, an equal-contribution note, and conference publication text. The overall section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds the granular-ablation Table 2, renumbering the previous Tables 2 and 3 as Tables 3 and 4. It adjusts some figure formatting and captions and reflows appendix figures relative to their discussion. The existing 32 figures are retained without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v5 adds potentially useful mechanistic tests, instruction-hierarchy validation, clearer wording, and concrete code-access instructions. However, new Table 2 attributes a 61% baseline ASR to gpt-oss-20b while retained Figure 18 reports 78.6%, without explaining different settings. The new 160-sample AUC study also leaves regression train/test separation and confidence-interval construction unspecified. These issues limit confidence in the principal added evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
